Class ServiceFiles

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.ServiceFiles
public final class ServiceFiles extends Object
Writes the service files ServiceLoader reads on the class path: META-INF/services/<service>, listing the implementations of a service, one binary name per line.

A processor registers implementations as it finds or generates them, in any round: 

ClassName mapper = ClassName.of(type).generatedNameWithSuffix("Mapper");
context.sources().write(JavaFile.newBuilder(mapper.packageName(), mapperType).build(), type);
context.services().add(ClassName.of("com.example", "Mapper"), mapper, type);

The filer creates each file once per compilation, so the files are written all at once, after the last round: a StepProcessor does it for its steps; any other processor calls write() when RoundEnvironment.processingOver() is true. A file that is already in the class output, as after an incremental build, keeps its entries, except those of a class that no longer exists. Each file lists every implementation once, sorted. Until then, discard(ClassName) withdraws the implementations of a service, so that its file is not written.

When it writes them, it checks that ServiceLoader can load each registered implementation: a public class, not abstract, top-level or static, that has a public constructor without parameters and is a subtype of the service. Each problem is reported as an error on the implementation. A service file is only read on the class path: a static provider() method, which only a module can use, does not replace the constructor.

On the module path, ServiceLoader ignores service files and reads the provides directives of the module declaration instead, which a processor cannot write. An implementation in a named module whose declaration does not provide it is reported as a warning, so that the module works on both paths. A processor that adds the provides directives itself after compilation, as by rewriting module-info.class, turns that check off with skipModuleCheck(ClassName).

  • Method Details

    • add

      public void add(ClassName service, ClassName implementation, Element... originatingElements)
      Registers an implementation of a service, to list in the service's file when the files are written. Registering it again only adds originating elements. Neither type needs to exist yet: the implementation may be generated in a later round.
      Parameters:
      service - the service, the interface or class ServiceLoader loads implementations of
      implementation - the implementation; a nested class is written with its binary name, as com.example.Outer$Inner
      originatingElements - the elements the registration comes from, so that incremental builds rewrite the file when they change
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the file of the service was already written

    • skipModuleCheck

      public void skipModuleCheck(ClassName service)
      Turns off the check that the module of each implementation of a service declares provides for it. No warning is reported then for an implementation in a named module whose declaration lacks the directive: for a processor that adds the directives after compilation, as by rewriting module-info.class with a bytecode tool. The other checks of the implementations still apply. Call it before the files are written, in any round, whether the service has implementations registered yet or not.
      Parameters:
      service - the service whose implementations are not checked against their module declaration
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the file of the service was already written, and so checked

    • discard

      public void discard(ClassName service)
      Discards the implementations registered for a service, so that its file is not written: for a processor that finds out, as late as in Step.processingOver(), that it must not write the file, as when the user wrote one by hand. An implementation registered after this is registered anew, and its service's file written. 
      public void processingOver() {
    if (hasHandWrittenServiceFile()) {
        context.services().discard(FACTORY);
        context.diagnostics().error("Remove " + FACTORY_FILE + ": the processor writes it");
    }
}

      A file of the service already in the class output, as from an earlier build, is left as it is, neither pruned nor deleted. The module check stays skipped if skipModuleCheck(ClassName) skipped it. Discarding a service without implementations registered does nothing.

      Parameters:
      service - the service whose implementations are discarded
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the file of the service was already written

    • write

      public void write()
      Checks the implementations registered since the files were last written, then writes the file of each service they implement. Call it after the last round: the filer refuses to create a file twice, so an implementation registered after its service's file is written cannot be added to it. A StepProcessor calls it for its steps.

      The entries of a file already in the class output are kept, and every entry is listed once, in the order of String.compareTo(String). A file another processor has created in this compilation cannot be read nor written, which is reported as an error.

      An entry of that file is dropped if its class no longer exists, as after an incremental build deleted it, since ServiceLoader would fail on it: when no type of the compilation, from its sources, class path or module path, has its binary name, and the class output has no class file for it either. An entry whose class file is still in the class output is kept, even when the class output is not on the class path of the compilation. Only the file of a service with implementations registered in the compilation is written, and so pruned.

      Throws:
      UncheckedIOException - if a file cannot be read or written
